Author: Lip Yong Lim
Review: Another one of them hipster places sprouting up along the Jonker area in Melaka. Author: Joelle C (Treasure Unity)

Author: Jackie Liew
Review: In the hustle bustle of Jonker walk sleeps a small establishment. The very entrance puzzles many upon entering. Greeting guest are folks from the olden days and an alter like backdrop making first impressions very hard to forget. Guts …MoreIn the hustle bustle of Jonker walk sleeps a small establishment. The very entrance puzzles many upon entering. Greeting guest are folks from the olden days and an alter like backdrop making first impressions very hard to forget. Guts shifts once you walk pass the first room into the next. Things seemed a bit foresty and cool. However, things are not so cool once you get past this as you will be greeted by bones and what shamans use to worship or curse.Once you sit down, accompanying you by your side can be a picture like mine which leaves one to think it may be another apparatus of worship for the jungle folks.The menu is a bit tattered but the content is very enticing. With prices ranging from RM 18 to RM 27.50, the burgers caught my eyes the most. They are not really your typical burgers and the descriptions failed to describe how glorious they taste. The spices and doness tickles the tounge. The portion is just right for one hungry hog. Well, if you're a hog then you shouldn't be eating till you drop. So learn to eat just enough to fill your tummy.The service is quick and even with a bunch of tourist, they serve at a pretty efficient speed. Before I end, the Melaka coffee is much stronger than the ones we find in coffee shops. Portion could be bigger but hey, I might be talking this much because of the coffee.Keep up the great standards. Maybe brighten up a bit. It's not always Halloween and babies might get scared.

Review: I've known about Baboon House for a while but never got there, due to not putting a high priority to go there as there's just so many food options in the area. …MoreI've known about Baboon House for a while but never got there, due to not putting a high priority to go there as there's just so many food options in the area.However this time around, while planning to head to one of the famous Kopitiams near Masjid Kapitan Keling, which was apparently closed for a few days, I recalled the recommendation of a friendly local Malaccan man from the night before who was recommending that we try the handmade burgers at Baboon house, so that's where my friend and I ended up at.My friend had the signature Baboon beef burger (they actually let you choose if you want a beef/chicken or pork patty) and I had the pork belly burger. Would've preferred if the burgers came with proper hand-cut fries though. That would defo make it a bang for your bucks.The coffee here is excellent too, by the way. Service was impeccable. Review: As many have posted the food is really good particularly the tapas. Oh we had the Gazpacho too (good but not great) as well as the iberico with roasted potatoes and three sauces. Nice smoky flavours on two of sauces but some of the meat was a little tough. I was hoping your food could redeem itself, unfortunately it just added more salt to the wound.The thing that ticks me off is your staff. Seriously, why can’t your staff be more warm and informative, informing us before hand that will be no straw served as part of the environment campaign. I am cool with that but please at least put a freaking sign if they are soo lazy to talk! I even asked for a hot water for my tea and it took ages for them to replenish it. This is a fine dining restaurant but with a low class service. Even at Mamak, they even provide BETTER service and treated their customers with a smile.I am not happy, dissatisfied and feeling regret for choosing this restaurant. No salute for you! Such a shame.A Very Dissapointed Customer,Azza AzizPetaling Jaya

This one is worth a stop in. …MoreColourfull decor and surroundings, filling and tasty food and proper hospitality. Having an evening walk by the river? This one is worth a stop in.I found this place through Google maps after finding that the bars opposite my hotel are closed until 7. On seeing previous reviews I decided on this place. It was a 5 minute stroll from my hotel up river past the striking multi coloured hotels and houses lying close each side of the river bank. There isn't a big flashy entrance but the waiters were quick to seat me outside. I ordered an ice coffee and  a water, the waiter misheard me and brought a mango lassi. On realising his mistake he was immediately apologetic and offered it for free which I have not experienced anywhere outside of the UK. Service I was so impressed with I offered to pay anyway. The lassi was top notch, super creamy and not too sweet with the yogurt.I moved inside to the open fronted side of the cafe which had a vine covered entrance and old musical memorabilia on the walls. The kind of chique I'm used to in my home town of bristol. and got a nasi lemak  with chicken rendang . The food was again, excellent. The rice was creamy with coconut and steamed with anise which complimented the rich curry chicken. The reduced chilli paste added sweetness and a tang (you don't need chilli to get a sweat on in Malaysia but it helps!) And the kimchi esque pickled veg added some crunch, as did the whole nuts. The food was more than enough.In total including two bottles of water and  forcibly paying for the lassi it was 25RM which I can't fault. I went back outside and spoke with the waiter and chef for a while about malacca and films (I'm not a big watcher but Malaysians seem to love film!)I don't dish out 5 stars too often but this is a winner.

Author: HM Choo

Author: David Harper
Review: Food was not too good and really do not like business tactics here. We ordered a squid dish, kang kong, a shrimp omelette, rice, a spring roll, a beer and an ice tea. When we sat down they brought some prawn chips to the table without …MoreFood was not too good and really do not like business tactics here. We ordered a squid dish, kang kong, a shrimp omelette, rice, a spring roll, a beer and an ice tea. When we sat down they brought some prawn chips to the table without asking and they also tried to give us wet towels toward the end which we told them we did not need. When we got out bill there were charges for the towels and the chips. I do not go back to restaurants like this where they try to rip off the patrons, even if the food was good, but in this case the food was very poor quality. The omelette was so greasy we did not even eat more than one bite. The spring roll was also greasy and mushy. The rice was not fresh. The squid was overcooked, and the kang kong was fishy tasting (and yes we like fish sauce).  The total bill for a bad lunch was 86.50 MYR. I did not argue with them - I speak with reviews and return business.  Bad business practices do not deserve business.

Author: Persona Altera
Review: Second time we’ve been to this Nyonya restaurant and they have been consistent with the delicious food. …MoreSecond time we’ve been to this Nyonya restaurant and they have been consistent with the delicious food.The rendang chicken was fragrant and spectacular.Both the calamari and pineapple prawn were fresh and definitely hits the spot.Their calamansi juice were handmade in their very own kitchen and not the conventional method of using syrup.This restaurant definitely stayed true to their Nyonya roots by using typical Malay spices with Chinese influences, and the flavors were comparatively sweeter as compared to their counterpart up at the Penang area or down at Singapore.However, we thought that their Cendol were slightly above average and there are much more room to improve on.Cost wise, for the five of us it set us back RM195 which is alright for a mid range restaurant.Their service was definitely better than before due to smaller customer crowd. Previously, we came in at around 1pm and encountered a line. So we had to stand outside to queue for about 30 mins andthey barely had time to serve us. But this time round, we arrive at 6:40pm and we could secure a table the moment we step into the restaurant. Author: Jeffrey Tan
Review: Somehow or rather all those ratings provided to this restaurant is not as expected and may not up to the standard requirements of rating a good restaurant with certain qualities or criteria requirements that the restaurant itself had graded …MoreSomehow or rather all those ratings provided to this restaurant is not as expected and may not up to the standard requirements of rating a good restaurant with certain qualities or criteria requirements that the restaurant itself had graded themselves in providing very good quality food, value added, fairness, reasonable portions of food, cleaniness, prices, sincerity and of course it's services. I may say some of those whom had over rated or had simply given a few extras stars to this restaurant may have yet to try other restaurants offering the same dishes. Let's begin with: Standard - it's a very simple Halal Restaurant that sells Chicken Rice Ball and others cuisines which is operated and owned by a Non Muslim whereby all it's staffs are Muslim which is not a problem at all for all Malaysian which is a good example of one Malaysia, Value Added - There's no added value that I and friends could really give a good positive tick for this shop. A small tables that normally can only accommodate 5 to maximum 6 persons would be offered to guest of 8 persons, so just imagine how crowded it is. The menu acclaimed that each table of customers can only order once and there shall be no additional order or top up will be entertained, which means should your order is not enough and would like to order extras, you need to pay the bill and walk out of the shop and start to que again. Thats something very funny and it's the first of such restrictions ever heard at any restaurant in Malaysia. Good Quality Food - Whatever food that this restaurant serves, you may find a much better taste somewhere else which would provides much better quality and much better taste which is much better quality. Fairness and Reasonable Portions of Food - Ordered a half chicken but provided a 3/4 chicken which comes with chicken wing but missing chicken drumsticks, an eggs omelettes that is just enough for 3 persons, a medium size Sambal Sotong that is just nice for 3 persons, 50 Chicken Rice Balls thats is much much smaller in size as compared to others Chicken Rice Balls Restaurant and the only correct portions of food serves is the Vegetables. Even normal individual Chicken Rice that's selling at coffeeshop has a bigger portions of Rice and Chicken Meat! Most people named this business methods as Ripped Off! Services - Services by the staffs is super fast and polite even though being repeatedly scolded by the business owner and for that reasons, thats where the second star is added on. Cleaniness is something that you don't expect to be perfect. As many experienced dinners claimed, the best method to judge the cleaniness of a restaurant or shops, is to survey the washroom and it's ingredients preparations areas. Prices we paid is exorbitant from our imagination. With those small portions of food served,we may say this is the most expensive Chicken Rice Balls Restaurant in Melaka. Even those few most famous Chicken Rice Balls Restaurant at Jonker Street or Melaka Sentral charges much cheaper and provide bigger portions of food as compared to this restaurant. But what really surprised me is that this restaurant is crowded with mostly Muslim eventhough it's food portions is small and it's charges is expensive. Surprise really surprised. Frankly, it's not really worth the money nor a good eating place to be recommended to friends, tourist or anyone. Don't believe? Try it than you'll judge it yourself

Author: Jay Chua
Review: Wanted to come here since long time ago, bucket list checked!We ordered the Itik Tim, jantung Pisang, babi cencaluk, nangka lemak, Ngoh Hiang …MoreWanted to come here since long time ago, bucket list checked!We ordered the Itik Tim, jantung Pisang, babi cencaluk, nangka lemak, Ngoh Hiang "fried spring roll" and cendol. First of all, cendol is among the best I tasted in Malaysia. They used traditional coarser shaved ice, the gula Melaka and the green bits are fragrant with no artificial smell.Jantung Pisang and babi cincaluk are salty by nature, they have very unique aroma and are exactly what you need to down your rice with. The nangka lemak served as a neutralizer with it's thick gravy and fibrous texture.Ngoh Hiang is simple and don't forget to dip into chili sauce for the complete taste. We're little bit disappointed by the itik Tim, as not much duck meat, mostly are bones, but soup tasted good nevertheless, just not so high value.It's not easy to eat so many dishes with each having their unique traits, kudos to the chef. Will definitely come again if craving for cendol.Ambient ⭐⭐⭐⭐Flavour ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐Value ⭐⭐⭐Locality ⭐⭐⭐⭐Cleanliness ⭐⭐⭐⭐All the above is just my personal opinion, "to know what honey tastes like, you have to try it one time".

Author: Shaun C

Review: Dissapointed, both the service and the foodVisiting during a peak holiday weekend, we were prepared to patiently queue up …MoreDissapointed, both the service and the foodVisiting during a peak holiday weekend, we were prepared to patiently queue up half an hour (5:30pm) before the dinner opening time (we were around 6th in line). Review: How would i describe Daorae ?1) The Place. Well, the dining areas are separated into 2 types. You can have …MoreHow would i describe Daorae ?1) The Place. Well, the dining areas are separated into 2 types. You can have private table area or you can have communal areas where you can hear everyone and everyone can hear you.  For intimate dining experience where you want a dinner for two experience with your partner/spouse, request the private tables. If you're going with a group of ppl, on the other hand, be it family reunion/gathering or friends gathering, ask for the communal area. The only thing is if you just walk-in, you're pretty much subject to whatever table is free at that time. I would highly recommend you call in advance & ask if you can reserve a table instead to avoid disappointment.2) The Service. Throughout my many visits here, I'd say, to be fair, it really depends on how busy they are. You must understand, at this restaurant, the staffs are the ones doing the cooking of you BBQ meat, in front of you. They also bring your food from the kitchen & top up your drinks & side dishes as you enjoy your food. So on very busy days, like CNY or PH, where there's a lot of customers, they'll definitely be overwhelmed time to time. So just call them as and when you need them. If you see that your meat is not very long to being charred, call the staff loudly & get him to attend to it, instead of sitting there quietly & letting your meat get charred. (They're not paid to entertain you alone! Be kind & be reasonable lar!) . On a normal lazy day, they staffs were quiet attentive & friendly.3) The Food... is DELICIOUS~!!! I love the BBQ porks & chicken~!!! I love the kimchi jjigae~!!! And i definitely love the endless side dishes~!!! Trust me, my wife & I have tried other similarly prices Korean BBQ place & no other place is like Daorae~!!! The only complaint I have if the staffs sometimes likes to rush things through. Perhaps this could be fixed with better training. For eg, we ordered Kimchi Jjigae, BBQ Pork & Chicken. The staff wanted to cook the chicken immediately after cooking the pork & we had to stop him from doing so. Otherwise the chicken would be cold by the time we finished the pork. I suspect they're trying to maximise the temperature of the coal but seriously, in some culture, this behaviour can be seen as the staff is trying to chase the customer away by rushing everything through. We come to this restaurant to enjoy our food and that mean sitting there, chit chatting while enjoy our food while it's still hot & delicious! I hope this could be improved.Well, overall, my wife & I love this place. Except for the few minor issues, this is actually a good place to spend & hour or two with you loved ones, enjoy delicious food & make beautiful memories with everyone. 4/5 Stars.

The portions are small because you get the option of ordering dishes in small or large sizes and the complainers ordered the small. At the counter bar corner, you can find various types of draft beer, whiskey and wine.Udang besar bakar @ Bert's Garden Seafood in Tanjung Kling Melaka.Bert's Garden Seafood, located along the coast overlooking the Straits of Malacca, offers a large selection of natural shrimp.Pronounced "Udang besar bakar" in Malay. Charcoal grilled simply by sprinkling salt on a large natural shrimp. Really delicious!Neither the central wholesale market in Malacca nor the large supermarket AEON sells such large and fresh shrimp.It seems that a long-time-related fisherman brings only large shrimp caught in the waters near the Straits of Malacca to Barts Garden.The price is reasonable, but... delicious!Not only prawns but also Malaysian sea bream (jenna), sea bream (shakup), large mud clubs, fresh squid, etc. You can choose your favorite seafood and sell it by weight and bake, steam or fried on the spot. You can cook with your favorite cooking method.The price is very reasonable because it is the market price of the day.Bert's Garden Seafood2078-C,, Jalan Kampung Pinang B, 76400 Tanjung Kling, Melaka(Original)マラッカで本格的なシーフードをリーズナブルな価格で味わえるレストランです。日没時にはマラッカ海峡に沈む夕日が独り占めできてしまう幸運な日もあります。エビやイカ、白身魚などフレッシュなシーフードを自分の目で見て選んで、塩焼きとかエビフライなどの調理方法を伝えて料理してもらうことも可能です。カウンターバーコーナーでは各種生ビールからウイスキーやワインも揃っています。Udang besar bakar @ Bert's Garden Seafood in Tanjung Kling Melaka.マラッカ海峡を望む海岸沿いに建つバーツガーデン（Bert's Garden Seafood）では、天然物の大型の海老が味わえます。マレー語で"Udang besar bakar"と綴り「ウダン・ブサ・バカール」と発音します。大きな天然海老に塩を振り掛けただけの炭火焼き。実に美味い！マラッカの中央卸売市場でも、大型スーパーのAEONさんでもこれだけ立派な大型で新鮮な海老は売っていません。長年つきあいのある漁師さんがマラッカ海峡近海で捕獲した大型の海老をバーツガーデンさんだけに持ち込んでくださるそうです。値段も、そこそこしますが･･･美味い！海老だけじゃなくマレーシアの鯛（ジェナ）や鱸（シャカップ）、大型のマッドクラブ、新鮮なイカなど自分の好きな海鮮シーフードを選んで量り売りしてもらい、その場で焼いたり、蒸したり、揚げたり好きな調理方法で料理していただけます。お値段は、その日の浜値（Market Price）なのでとってもリーズナブルですぞ。Bert's Garden Seafood2078-C,, Jalan Kampung Pinang B, 76400 Tanjung Kling, Melaka

Author: Tony Kansai
Review: (Translated by Google) Probably the best vegetarian restaurant "古" Ku Cha Be @ Jalan Kota Laksamana Melaka. …More(Translated by Google) Probably the best vegetarian restaurant "古" Ku Cha Be @ Jalan Kota Laksamana Melaka.Perhaps I found a vegetarian restaurant in Malacca that best suits Japanese tastes. When I was invited by an acquaintance, I stopped by for lunch at a restaurant where I wrote "Koya" in English and "Ku Cha Be" in English.It is recommended that it is a specialty food, Thunder Tea Rice (Thunder Tea Rice). Many people know that if you ask Hakka Rui-cha (Hakka Rui-cha), you will be blessed with mint-flavored herbs and green tea in a five-grain rice with plenty of vegetables.Vegetables are lined up so that long beans, Korean greens, soybeans, daikon radish, sesame seeds, red beans, and rapeseed serve five grains of rice. First of all, let's taste the taste of the first minced vegetables with five grains rice with mog mog.Next, we sprinkle herb green tea and mix it in a tea pickled style. Herb green tea is a blend of nine layers tower, thin leaf (mint herb), puar tea, white sesame and red beans. It is recommended that you taste each dish twice with different ways of eating.At the same time, the taste of herbs and green tea differs depending on the store, even for Hakka Ruicha. Basically, it is characterized by the smell of mint herbs, but in Malacca it is so light that you can wear a shoulder mark as "Eh?"However, "Choraya" Ku Cha Be's herb green tea is seasoned with a taste of saltiness and taste for the Japanese taste. At the beginning, I wrote "It is a vegetarian restaurant that best suits the tastes of Japanese people in Malacca" because it's a crispy dish with a salty taste.Well, let's explain the place of the shop. It is about 7-8 minutes by car from the city center of Melaka. You can walk, but it is 30 minutes (about 2 km) walk from Clock Tower Square, so it is recommended to access by taxi or grab.(Original)Probably the best vegetarian restaurant "古早味" Ku Cha Be @ Jalan Kota Laksamana Melaka.おそらく、マラッカでいちばん日本人の好みに合うベジタリアンレストランを発見しました。知人に誘われてランチを食べに立ち寄ったのは、漢字で「古早味」と書いて、英語では "Ku Cha Be" と綴り「くちゃべ」と発音するレストランです。名物料理だと奨められたのは、サンダーティーライス （ Thunder Tea Rice ）。客家擂茶（ハッカ・ルイチャ）と聞けばご存じの方も多いと思いますが、野菜たっぷりの五穀米ごはんに、ミント風味のハーブ・グリーンティーをぶっかけてお茶漬け風にしていただきます。長豆、高麗菜、大豆、大根、胡麻、小豆、菜心が五穀米ごはんをとりまくように野菜が並んでいます。まず、最初に細かく刻まれた野菜を五穀米ごはんと一緒にモグモグと食し風味を味わいましょう。次に、ハーブグリーンティーをぶっかけて、お茶漬け風に混ぜながらいただきます。ハーブ･グリーンティーは九層塔、薄荷葉（ミントハーブ）、プアール茶、白胡麻に小豆などがブレンドされています。それぞれに美味い、異なる食べ方で２度美味さを味わうがおすすめだそうです。同じ、客家擂茶（ハッカ・ルイチャ）でも、お店によってハーブ・グリーンティーの味が異なります。基本的にミントのハーブの香りが特徴なんですが、マラッカでは「えぇ？」と肩すかしを喰らうほど薄味なのです。ところが "古早味" Ku Cha Be さんのハーブグリーンティーは塩味のさじ加減が日本人の好みの味付けなんです。冒頭に「マラッカでいちばん日本人の好みに合うベジタリアンレストラン」と書いたのは、塩味がキチンとついてるメリハリのある料理だからなのです。さて、お店の場所を説明しておきましょう。マラッカの街の中心部から、クルマで約７～８分の場所にあります。歩いてもいいですが、時計台広場から歩くと30分（約2km）あるので、タクシーかグラブでアクセスするのをおすすめします。

Author: Jojoe Ali
Review: Some locals might claim that the asam pedas isn't authentic enough, but to me it is good enough. In fact, could be among the best ones. I also love the fact that they're the only one to serve the set with cooked cabbage (lauk sayur kubis) …MoreSome locals might claim that the asam pedas isn't authentic enough, but to me it is good enough. In fact, could be among the best ones. I also love the fact that they're the only one to serve the set with cooked cabbage (lauk sayur kubis) instead of typical ulam.And even if you're not a fan of asam pedas, there's plenty of other options like kerang rebus, street burger, roti john, fried noodles etc; which tasted just as goooood.Some also claim that the price is slightly on the higher side. Well, it isn't cheap, but totally not expensive either (standard price like those local food restaurants in KL). I was charged RM23 for a set of one claypot bowl of Asam Pedas Telur Ikan Tenggiri (two big fish roe; more than enough for two), a plate of hot rice (not cold and dry like some street restaurants), cabbage, sambal belacan and salted egg + one roti canai + ice lemon tea + sirap limau. I believe, if it's in KL, RM23 might just be enough for the asam pedas telur ikan alone. Lol.And the claim that the service is bad is also baseless. There were plenty of waiters, and quite fast too. Yes, the turnaround time for a meal to be sent to your table could be improved, but to the extent that you turned restless by it.Oh.. this is not one of those fancy restaurants, fyi. It is just a typical shophouse, 2 or 3 lots combined, with the small alley in front of it filled up with dozens of tables. Yet still, the ambience is cool enough, considering there is no nice views (well.. you don't really need in the dark lol). There's a busker band too (tho they might wanna consider looking for a new better vocalist, but that's a whole different topic lol).All in all, I would definitely come here every time I'm in Melaka. It is just a walk away from Casa Del Rio, aka not too far from Jonker area. Opens at 6pm and closes at 4pm. Highly recommended.
Restaurant: Asam Pedas Claypot 2 Restoran Kota Laksamana
Location: 86, Jalan Laksamana 5, Taman Kota Laksamana, Malacca

We were lucky to find a small table to accommodate ourselves.So we ordered our food, i took Daging Tetel asam pedas and my wife Pari Asam Pedas. The set gives us sambal, rice, some veggies, telur masin. Also got the chance to order 2 basket of my favourite otak otak which i still think Melaka have the best taste compared to other states (yea abit bias bout the otak otak).It took roughly 30 minutes for out food to arrive considering the shop is at full capacity when we first arrived. Now, while im not a big fan of Asam Pedas as i said earlier, this shop managed to convinced me otherwise. Damn it was good... Surely the presentation looks normal and uninspiring but heck the food was damn tasty!! Been awhile since i ate outside and had great cheap food like this and make my taste buds go crazy.  Their reputation surely isnt something to look down upon. Yes they are legit.Tl;DR if you want to have a good experience in Asam Pedas.. this is a great place to have some!!!! You wont regret it.
